newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures up, June become benchmark.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures up, June become benchmark.

text.p: June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures inched up in thin trade on Tuesday, as uncertainty over Japan's general election on Sunday prevented any significant movement.

The June contract inherited the benchmark status of futures contracts, as its volume has exceeded that of the ongoing benchmark March contract for two days in a row. The June contract's volume was 19,841 contracts.

This compares with the March contract's 16,759 contracts. The March contract had been the benchmark for only about one-and-a-half months, the shortest time on record that a contract has stayed as a benchmark.
Dealers said the March became immobile, as it had been bought continuously near its limit in the recent uptrend which started in August, while there were no good reasons to sell.
The June contract moved in a narrow range between 99.13 and 99.16. Many dealers said it was unlikely to move until the general election result became clear.

In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate mostly stood at 0.49 percent, up 0.02 from Monday. As Tuesday was the last day of the current bank reserve reporting period, fund demand was tighter than usual, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) drained 400 billion yen from the market in its morning operation to balance fund conditions.

The overnight call rate has tended to fall on the last day in the past several reporting periods due to ample BOJ fund supply. As the BOJ had kept a neutral stance throughout the reporting period this time, the tendency was again for the rate to rise on the last day, a trader at a city bank said.
Rates in the open market were steady, with benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) issued at an unchanged 0.52 percent. About 95 billion yen worth of issues had been reported.

"Many investors seem to be waiting to see the market trend in the next reporting period starting tomorrow... They have no reason to let out funds hastily today," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank.
About 40 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.49 percent, the same rate as Monday's. Two-month CDs were unchanged at 0.50 percent, with 10 billion yen worth issued.
